sentences.en: It's a Saturday afternoon in Golden Gate Park, and a handful of kids are taking turns sending a little white stomp rocket into the gray San Francisco sky.
sentences.zh: 这是一个周六的下午，在金门公园，几个孩子轮流把一个白色的小型踩踏火箭发射到旧金山灰蒙蒙的天空中。

sentences.en: It arcs up, then sails back down to this small meadow at the northern edge of the park, bounded by shaggy evergreens.
sentences.zh: 它划出一道弧线，然后落回到公园北缘的一片小草地上，四周环绕着茂密的常青树。

sentences.en: Yeah, so the rocket lands, the kids go apeshit, then they proceed to tear off after it,
sentences.zh: 火箭落地了，孩子们兴奋得发疯，接着他们就追着火箭跑去，

sentences.en: fully oblivious to the tall, thin man watching from atop a nearby boulder.
sentences.zh: 完全没注意到附近一块巨石上正站着一个高瘦的男人在看着他们。
那是制片人克里斯·科林。

sentences.en: The man is made of bronze, and this obscure little corner of the park is named for him.
sentences.zh: 这个男人是青铜做的，公园里这个不起眼的小角落就是以他的名字命名的。

sentences.en: The Doughboy statue was unveiled here in the Doughboy Meadow in 1930.
sentences.zh: “面团男孩”雕像于1930年在这里的“面团男孩草地”揭幕。

sentences.en: He's a handsome young guy gazing out resolutely at the patch of earth that has borne his name for almost a century.
sentences.zh: 他是一个英俊的年轻人，坚定地注视着这片以他的名字命名了近一个世纪的土地。

sentences.en: I was just curious about one thing, so I walked up to a couple sitting near the stomp rocket kids.
sentences.zh: 我只是对一件事感到好奇，于是我走到坐在踩踏火箭的孩子们附近的一对夫妇身边。

sentences.en: Hey, can I ask you guys a question?
sentences.zh: 嘿，能问你们一个问题吗？

sentences.en: Do you know who that is?
Do you know what a Doughboy is?
sentences.zh: 你知道什么是面团男孩吗？

sentences.en: I just knew this was Doughboy Meadow's deductive reasoning.
sentences.zh: 我只知道这是面团男孩草地，这是演绎推理。

sentences.en: I present this high-level exchange because it illustrates something about our world.
sentences.zh: 我展示这段高水平的对话，是因为它说明了我们世界的一些情况。

sentences.en: Specifically the bronze and granite corner of our world,
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是我们世界中青铜和花岗岩的角落，

sentences.en: where we memorialize the losses most important to us as a civilization.
sentences.zh: 在那里，我们纪念作为文明社会对我们最重要的损失。

sentences.en: The Doughboy Meadow commemorates 39 San Franciscans who were killed in World War I.
sentences.zh: 面团男孩草地纪念了39名在第一次世界大战中阵亡的旧金山人。

sentences.en: 16 more were killed in World War II, and their names were added to the plaque under the statue.
sentences.zh: 又有16人在第二次世界大战中阵亡，他们的名字被加到了雕像下的牌匾上。

sentences.en: Doughboys are what they used to call infantrymen back in the day.
sentences.zh: “面团男孩”是过去人们对步兵的称呼。

sentences.en: A fact that nobody Chris interviewed on the meadow that morning seemed to know.
sentences.zh: 那天早上克里斯在草地上采访的似乎没人知道这个事实。

sentences.en: But it raises questions in your mind about the purpose of memorials.
sentences.zh: 但这让你对纪念碑的目的产生了疑问。

sentences.en: Or at least it does if, like me, you've spent the last year walking up to every memorial you see,
sentences.zh: 或者至少如果你像我一样，过去一年里一直在走近你看到的每一座纪念碑，

sentences.en: and wondering what they say about us, and wondering what they even do.
sentences.zh: 想知道它们在诉说着我们什么，甚至想知道它们到底有什么用，你就会有这种疑问。

sentences.en: So that's partly why I wandered over to the Doughboy Meadow that Saturday.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我那个周六漫步到面团男孩草地的部分原因。

sentences.en: But I have to admit something to you, which is that this story is not about Doughboys.
sentences.zh: 但我必须向你承认一件事，那就是这个故事不是关于面团男孩的。

sentences.en: In fact, this whole scene in the Doughboy Meadow has allowed me to put off mentioning something
sentences.zh: 事实上，面团男孩草地的整个场景让我推迟了提到某件事，

sentences.en: that I fear will make you yank out your earbuds the moment I bring it up.
sentences.zh: 我担心一旦我提起它，你就会立刻拔掉耳机。

sentences.en: This is actually a story about COVID.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一个关于新冠的故事。

sentences.en: And more specifically, it's about a group of people fighting to create a memorial
sentences.zh: 更具体地说，它是关于一群人努力为一种毁灭性的疾病建立纪念碑，

sentences.en: for a devastating disease that many of us just don't want to talk about or think about anymore.
sentences.zh: 而我们许多人已经不想再谈论或思考这种疾病了。

sentences.en: He was a very handsome guy.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常英俊的人。

sentences.en: I don't know why that just made me sad.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么这让我感到难过。

sentences.en: He's wearing his quintessential early 90s gear, which includes aviators, you know, off-brand Ray-Bans,
sentences.zh: 他穿着典型的90年代初的装备，包括飞行员墨镜，你知道的，非名牌的雷朋，

sentences.en: a polo shirt, and these, like, tiny little McGregor shorts
sentences.zh: 一件Polo衫，还有这些，像麦格雷戈那种超短裤，

sentences.en: that are, like, made out of vinyl or something really interesting.
sentences.zh: 是用乙烯基或者其他什么非常有趣的东西做的。

sentences.en: And he's got, like, the knee-high socks.
So he's just in this gazebo, sort of, like, beckoning me to come and be with him.
sentences.zh: 他就站在凉亭里，好像在招手让我过去陪他。

sentences.en: Kristen grew up with her dad and mom in Phoenix.
sentences.zh: 克里斯汀和她的父母在凤凰城长大。

sentences.en: They lived in a neighborhood called Maryville,
sentences.zh: 他们住在一个叫玛丽维尔的社区，

sentences.en: a working-class community that's largely immigrant and mostly Latino.
sentences.zh: 一个主要是移民和拉丁裔的工人阶级社区。

sentences.en: And that's where Kristen's parents were still living in 2020,
sentences.zh: 2020年，当世界第一次听到“冠状病毒”这个词时，克里斯汀的父母仍然住在那里，

sentences.en: when the world first heard the word coronavirus.
At first, the family was on the same page about this mysterious new disease.
sentences.zh: 起初，全家人对这种神秘的新疾病看法一致。

sentences.en: And then Trump decided to visit Arizona on May 5th.
sentences.zh: 然后特朗普决定在5月5日访问亚利桑那州。

sentences.en: And I think that was a political move to go and declare that we were on the right path.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是一个政治举动，去宣布我们走在正确的道路上。

sentences.en: Then the governor of Arizona went on a PR spree across the state,
sentences.zh: 接着亚利桑那州州长在全州进行了一场公关活动，

sentences.en: saying that it was safe to go about normal.
sentences.zh: 说恢复正常生活是安全的。

sentences.en: And that's when my relationship, when my conversations,
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我的关系，我的谈话，

sentences.en: when everything with my dad started to change.
sentences.zh: 我和我父亲之间的一切都开始改变了。

sentences.en: A couple things about her dad, Mark Urquiza.
sentences.zh: 关于她父亲马克·乌尔基扎的几件事。

sentences.en: One, he was a Fox News-watching, America-loving guy.
sentences.zh: 第一，他是一个看福克斯新闻、热爱美国的家伙。

sentences.en: If the guys he elected said COVID was under control for healthy people, he believed it.
sentences.zh: 如果他选出的那些人说新冠对健康人来说是可以控制的，他就相信。

sentences.en: He was happy and sweet and exuberant with this big voice.
sentences.zh: 他快乐、甜美、热情，嗓门很大。

sentences.en: And if anyone was at the edge of the room,
sentences.zh: 如果有人在房间的角落里，

sentences.en: he made sure they felt part of things.
sentences.zh: 他会确保他们感到自己是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: So-and-so's birthday or an important NASCAR race or any occasion in which to celebrate.
sentences.zh: 某某的生日，或者一场重要的纳斯卡赛车比赛，或者任何值得庆祝的场合。

sentences.en: Like, my dad was such a booster for experiencing joy.
sentences.zh: 我父亲真是个享受快乐的推动者。

sentences.en: So Mark didn't hesitate when a friend threw a birthday karaoke party
sentences.zh: 所以当一位朋友举办生日卡拉OK派对时，马克毫不犹豫地去了，

sentences.en: not long after Arizona's stay-at-home orders were lifted.
sentences.zh: 那是在亚利桑那州的居家令解除后不久。

sentences.en: Within a few weeks, Mark Urquiza was in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 几周之内，马克·乌尔基扎就住进了医院。

sentences.en: And though he was otherwise healthy, his condition worsened.
sentences.zh: 尽管他身体状况良好，但病情还是恶化了。

sentences.en: He got moved to the ICU.
sentences.zh: 他被转到了重症监护室。

sentences.en: And then, all alone, he was put on a ventilator.
sentences.zh: 然后，他独自一人被戴上了呼吸机。

sentences.en: Kristen was driving to Phoenix from her home in San Francisco on June 30th
sentences.zh: 6月30日，克里斯汀正从旧金山的家中开车前往凤凰城，

sentences.en: when she learned he was slipping away.
sentences.zh: 这时她得知父亲快不行了。

sentences.en: At a gas station on the side of the highway,
sentences.zh: 在高速公路旁的一个加油站，

sentences.en: she spoke to her father as a nurse at the hospital held up a phone to his ear.
sentences.zh: 她和父亲通了话，当时医院的一名护士把手机贴在他的耳边。

sentences.en: Mark was a high school 400-meter dash state champion and cross-country runner.
sentences.zh: 马克曾是高中400米短跑州冠军和越野跑运动员。

sentences.en: Mark was known for his infectious energy, strong will, and yes, stubbornness.
sentences.zh: 马克以其富有感染力的活力、坚强的意志，当然还有固执而闻名。

sentences.en: This is the obituary Kristen wrote for her father.
sentences.zh: 这是克里斯汀为她父亲写的讣告。

sentences.en: And then, it takes a turn.
sentences.zh: 然后，它发生了一个转折。

sentences.en: Mark, like so many others, should not have died from COVID-19.
sentences.zh: 像许多其他人一样，马克本不应该死于新冠肺炎。

sentences.en: His death is due to the carelessness of the politicians
sentences.zh: 他的死归咎于政客们的粗心大意，

sentences.en: who continue to jeopardize the health of brown bodies
sentences.zh: 他们继续通过明显的领导力缺失、

sentences.en: through a clear lack of leadership,
sentences.zh: 拒绝承认这场危机的严重性，

sentences.en: refusal to acknowledge the severity of this crisis,
sentences.zh: 以及无法也无意就如何降低风险给出明确和果断的指导，

sentences.en: and inability and unwillingness to give clear and decisive direction
sentences.zh: 而危及棕色人种的健康。
克里斯汀不仅悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: Kristen wasn't just beside herself with grief.

sentences.zh: 那篇讣告产生了一些非凡的效果。

sentences.en: And the obituary did something kind of remarkable.
sentences.zh: 它邀请任何有亲人遭受新冠折磨

sentences.en: It invited anyone with loved ones suffering from COVID

sentences.zh: 加入她在亚利桑那州议会大厦外建立的祭坛。

sentences.en: to join an altar she was creating outside the Arizona state capitol.
sentences.zh: 2020年7月，还没有人真正表达过这种悲伤和愤怒。

sentences.en: In July of 2020, nobody had really articulated this kind of sadness and anger yet.
sentences.zh: 那篇讣告在互联网上炸开了锅。

sentences.en: The obit exploded across the internet.
sentences.zh: 很快，州长就被问及马克的死。

sentences.en: Soon, the governor was being asked about Mark's death.
sentences.zh: 到了8月，克里斯汀通过Zoom在民主党全国代表大会上发言。

sentences.en: By August, Kristen was speaking by Zoom at the Democratic National Convention.
sentences.zh: 我父亲是一位健康的65岁老人。
他唯一的既往病史就是信任唐纳德·特朗普，

sentences.en: His only pre-existing condition was trusting Donald Trump,
sentences.zh: 为此，他付出了生命的代价。

sentences.en: and for that, he paid with his life.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这听起来像是要演变成一场反特朗普的抨击。

sentences.en: Okay, this sounds like it's winding up into an anti-Trump harangue.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，克里斯汀的生活基本上就是一场反特朗普的抨击。

sentences.en: For a minute, Kristen's life was basically an anti-Trump harangue.
sentences.zh: 但当这一切发生时，背景中还有其他事情正在发生。

sentences.en: But as that was going on, something else was happening in the background.
sentences.zh: 普通人开始联系克里斯汀。

sentences.en: Ordinary people started reaching out to Kristen.
sentences.zh: 在这位直言不讳的39岁非营利组织工作者身上，
他们看到了一个理解这个国家到底发生了什么的人。

sentences.en: they saw someone who grasped what was really happening in this country.
sentences.zh: 几十个，然后几百个，最终成千上万的陌生人

sentences.en: Dozens, and then hundreds, and eventually thousands of strangers
sentences.zh: 开始与她分享他们的悲伤。

sentences.en: began to share their grief with her.
sentences.zh: 我不认为世界上有任何人

sentences.en: I don't think there's anybody in the entire world
sentences.zh: 比我交谈过更多失去亲人的人。

sentences.en: who's talked to as many folks who've lost a loved one to COVID than me.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这是我从很多人那里听到的关于克里斯汀的话。

sentences.en: That's something I've heard from a number of people about Kristen, incidentally.
And the more people she heard from,
sentences.zh: 她的观点就开始发生演变。

sentences.en: the more her view began to evolve.
sentences.zh: 当时新冠占据了头条新闻。

sentences.en: COVID was dominating the headlines at the time.
sentences.zh: 那是每个人都在谈论的话题。

sentences.en: It was all anyone talked about.
sentences.zh: 然而，我们仍然没有真正面对

sentences.en: And yet, we still weren't really reckoning
sentences.zh: 它给世界带来的那种纯粹、可怕的损失。

sentences.en: with the amount of sheer, horrific loss
sentences.zh: 所有这些死亡显然是我们对新冠恐惧的核心。

sentences.en: it was grinding into the world.
sentences.zh: 但矛盾的是，我们还没有创造一个空间

sentences.en: All this death was obviously central to our fears about COVID.
sentences.zh: 或一个地方来纪念那些真正死去的人。

sentences.en: But paradoxically, we hadn't created a space
sentences.zh: 克里斯汀觉得，除非我们这样做，

sentences.en: or a place to honor the actual people who were dying.
sentences.zh: 否则这个国家永远不会真正痊愈。

sentences.en: Kristen felt like, until we did,
sentences.zh: 这也意味着它不会学会在下一次做得更好。

sentences.en: the country was never really going to heal.
sentences.zh: 克里斯汀沉浸在悲伤中。

sentences.en: Which also meant it wasn't going to learn to do better the next time.
sentences.zh: 但有一件事突然变得清晰起来。
有人需要为后代铭记这场灾难。

sentences.en: But one thing felt suddenly clear.
sentences.zh: 当然，无数更小、更本地化的纪念碑已经涌现。

sentences.en: Someone needed to mark this catastrophe

sentences.zh: 但克里斯汀想要一个全国性和历史性的规模。

sentences.en: Countless smaller and more local memorials have sprung up, of course.
sentences.zh: 一个为整个国家建立的永久性新冠纪念碑。
它需要像大流行本身一样宏大。

sentences.en: But Kristen wanted something national and historic in scope.
sentences.zh: 并且足够灵活，以适应仍在发展的疾病。

sentences.en: A permanent COVID memorial for the whole country.
sentences.zh: 并且足够深刻，能够认识到

sentences.en: It needed to be as big as the pandemic itself.
sentences.zh: 它如何加剧了国内的其他社会危机。

sentences.en: And flexible enough to accommodate a still unfolding disease.
sentences.zh: 并且足够复杂，能够以某种方式反映
我们最终会对这场大流行产生的所有截然不同的感受。

sentences.en: how it exacerbated other societal crises in the country.
sentences.zh: 所以，她决定给美国纪念部打电话。

sentences.en: And sophisticated enough to somehow reflect
sentences.zh: 他们立即开始着手创建一个永久性的纪念项目。

sentences.en: all of the wildly different feelings we'd eventually have
sentences.zh: 我们最终会对这场大流行产生的所有截然不同的感受。
所以，她决定给美国纪念部打电话。

sentences.en: So, she decided to call the United States Department of Memorialization.
sentences.zh: 他们立即开始着手创建一个永久性的纪念项目。

sentences.en: And they got right to work creating a permanent
sentences.zh: 他们立即开始着手创建一个永久性的纪念项目。

sentences.en: and very thoughtful national memorial to the COVID pandemic.
sentences.zh: 以及一个非常深思熟虑的全国性新冠疫情纪念碑。

sentences.en: Except, there is no Department of Memorialization.
sentences.zh: 只不过，并没有所谓的“纪念事务部”。

sentences.en: When, say, a highway gets made,
sentences.zh: 比方说，当要修建一条高速公路时，

sentences.en: there's a clear and consistent process for doing so.
sentences.zh: 有一套清晰且一贯的流程。
但公共纪念碑却并非如此。

sentences.en: From the Vietnam Wall to the National Memorial for Peace and Justice,
sentences.zh: 从越战纪念碑到国家和平与正义纪念碑，

sentences.en: Sometimes a handful of concerned citizens get together and make it happen.
sentences.zh: 有时是一群忧心忡忡的公民聚在一起促成此事。

sentences.en: Sometimes a non-profit pushes for it or a foundation.
sentences.zh: 有时则是由非营利组织或基金会来推动。

sentences.en: There's usually a lot of activism and a lot of fraught conversations
sentences.zh: 通常会伴随着大量的行动主义和充满张力的对话，

sentences.en: about design, location, the story it should tell about what happened
sentences.zh: 讨论关于设计、选址，以及它应该讲述一段怎样的故事，

sentences.en: And ideally, there's a whole other set of conversations
sentences.zh: 理想情况下，还会有一整套其他的讨论，

sentences.en: about whose perspectives are being reflected
sentences.zh: 关于哪些视角被呈现了出来，

sentences.en: and what unspoken agendas are embedding themselves in the project.
sentences.zh: 以及有哪些未言明的议程被植入到了项目中。

sentences.en: When you discuss a memorial or when you conceive a memorial,
sentences.zh: 当你讨论或构思一座纪念碑时，

sentences.en: sometimes the most productive part of it is the discussion itself.
sentences.zh: 有时最有成效的部分恰恰是讨论本身。

sentences.en: This is Marianne Hirsch, a Columbia professor
sentences.zh: 这位是玛丽安·赫希（Marianne Hirsch），哥伦比亚大学的一位教授，

sentences.en: who does a lot of work in memory studies
sentences.zh: 她在记忆研究领域做了大量工作，

sentences.en: and how we remember cultural trauma.
sentences.zh: 研究我们如何记忆文化创伤。

sentences.en: Because that is where we try to figure out as a community
sentences.zh: 因为正是通过这些讨论，我们作为一个社区，

sentences.en: or as a set of communities what happened
sentences.zh: 或者作为一群社区，试图弄清楚发生了什么，

sentences.en: and how we want to remember it,
sentences.zh: 以及我们想要如何铭记它，

sentences.en: but also how we want to remember it for the future.
sentences.zh: 同时也包括我们希望未来如何铭记它。

sentences.en: There are more than 48,000 monuments and memorials in this country.
sentences.zh: 在这个国家有超过48000座纪念碑和纪念物。

sentences.en: And as we've all learned in recent years,
sentences.zh: 正如我们近年来所了解到的，

sentences.en: that can very well mean 48,000 arguments
sentences.zh: 这很可能意味着有48000场争论，

sentences.en: about what they should and shouldn't be commemorating.
sentences.zh: 关于它们应该或不应该纪念什么。

sentences.en: Well, it's an interesting time to discuss this question
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在讨论这个问题很有意思，

sentences.en: because we're in the midst of memory wars in this country, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我们正处于这个国家的“记忆战争”之中，对吧？
